deep.reconstruction:
Context: in these 1983 'Teichmüller' notes Grothendieck works out explicit combinatorial (cellular, 'dessin'-type) models for small-genus cases. This page treats the equianharmonic elliptic curve E (j = 0, E = C/Z[ρ], ρ = e^{2πi/3}), which has Aut(E, e) ≅ Z/6Z, together with its quotient by the involution −1.

(1) The previous step, partly on the preceding page, uses a hexagonal fundamental domain cut by its diagonals. The page notes that in this cellular picture one again finds the three points of order 2 distinct from the origin e. These are E[2] \ {e}, the fixed points of −1 other than e.

(2) 'Doubling' the decomposition means refining it so that all four 2-torsion points become vertices. This gives the triangulation of the torus induced by the triangular lattice ½Λ:
- V = 4 (namely E[2]), E = 12, F = 8 equilateral triangles;
- χ = 4 − 12 + 8 = 0, as it must be for a torus;
- every vertex has degree 6.
The '8 arêtes' was corrected to 12 on the page. This is the regular toroidal map {3,6}_{2,0}. The partial drawing shows a hexagon whose upper triangles are subdivided by halving.

(3) Quotient by ±1. The involution −1 fixes exactly the four vertices. It acts freely on edges and faces: between each pair of vertices there are 2 edges, and −1 swaps them. The quotient E/±1 ≅ P^1 (the x-coordinate of the Weierstrass model) therefore receives:
- 4 vertices (one distinguished, the image of e);
- 6 edges joining the vertices pairwise;
- 4 triangular faces.
This is the tetrahedron, χ = 2. The degree-3 vertices correspond to cone angle π, i.e. the 4 branch points of the double cover E → P^1.

(4) Symmetry check. Orientation-preserving symmetries of the tetrahedron fixing a vertex form Z/3Z. This matches Aut(E, e)/±1 ≅ Z/6Z/±1 ≅ Z/3Z; hence the 'OK !'.

Purpose: this is a sanity check of the dictionary between curves with large automorphism groups (special points of moduli, here j = 0) and regular maps/polyhedra. It lets one see concretely how the 'cellular' model passes to the quotient by the elliptic involution. It is part of the combinatorial approach to Teichmüller/moduli spaces and to dessins d'enfants that Grothendieck developed in 1983–84.
errors: No mathematical errors. The self-correction 8 → 12 edges is right: with V = 4 and F = 8 triangles, 3F = 2E forces E = 12, and χ = 0.

Minor: the first line ('diagonales des 6 hexagones'?) is hard to read. The three order-2 points are best described as the 2-torsion points, i.e. the midpoints of the lattice translations, not literally points on the diagonals. The exact cellular picture of the previous step cannot be fully verified from this page alone.

ideas.what: Triangulation of the j = 0 torus by the half-lattice: 4 vertices (the 2-torsion points), 12 edges, 8 triangles; the regular toroidal map {3,6}_{2,0}
ideas.modern_name: regular map {3,6}_{2,0} on the torus; clean dessin / Belyi triangulation of the equianharmonic curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Coxeter–Moser, regular maps on the torus); in dessin language Grothendieck's school (Shabat–Voevodsky, Jones–Singerman)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses regular maps and tori with j = 0, 1728 in general terms; this specific computation is not known to me in print

ideas.what: Quotient of the torus by the elliptic involution ±1 is the tetrahedron, with the 4 vertices the branch points of x : E → P^1
ideas.modern_name: elliptic curve as double cover of P^1 branched at 4 points; tetrahedral dessin on the sphere
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weierstrass / Klein); tetrahedral picture standard in dessin literature
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (regular polyhedra, Platonic dessins)

ideas.what: Matching automorphism groups: Aut(E, e)/±1 ≅ Z/6/±1 ≅ Z/3 equals the orientation-preserving stabilizer of a vertex of the tetrahedron
ideas.modern_name: automorphism group of a pointed regular map vs. automorphisms of the curve

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, elementary worked example (the j = 0 torus triangulated by its 2-torsion points, whose quotient by −1 is the tetrahedron) of the kind central to the dessins-d'enfants programme. It is historically interesting as a trace of the 1983 genesis of that programme, but mathematically classical and well represented in the later literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'diagonales de l'hexagone, on a encore ces trois pts d'ordre 2 distincts de e' rather than 'des 6 hexagones'. The trailing word is uncertain.
'une cellulation avec 4 sommets' is plausible; the edge count was first written 8 and overwritten to 12.
The phrase transcribed 'obtenu tétraèdre' is more likely 'c'est le tétraèdre ordinaire (orienté)', with '(orienté)' inserted above the line.
Last line: the struck word before '≃' is probably 'groupe' or 'pour' (struck through); the formula reads '≃ Z/6Z / ±1, OK !'.
